To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the Euclidean structure is a special case of non-Euclidean structures and that (2) deep neural networks can be generalized to non-Euclidean domains.

(1) the invariances that are built into Euclidean convolutional neural networks can be replaced by invariances that reflect the underlying geometry of non-Euclidean domains and (2) the resulting networks are more powerful and more efficient than existing alternatives.

(i) the success of neural networks is not due to their non-linearity but to the inductive bias they encode; (ii) the most important inductive bias in neural networks is that they are translation invariant and equivariant to rotation; (iii) the inductive bias can be encoded in the architecture of the networks, and this can be done in an efficient way that does not increase the number of parameters.
